learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to independently conceive, perform, and critically evaluate complex mechanical calculations using FE programs.
Students can specifically apply numerical simulation tools (such as Abaqus and pyLabFEA) for structural analysis.

Students have developed a fundamental understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of linear and nonlinear elasticity as well as plasticity and can implement them practically using numerical methods.
Students can recognize data-based approaches to material modeling and apply them exemplarily to flow rules.

syllabus_topics: Basic principle of the finite element (FE) method using planar bar elements: stiffness matrix, setting up and solving the system of equations, evaluation
Linear elasticity theory: stress tensor, strain tensor, elasticity law, principle of virtual work
Finite elements in elasticity theory: development of a mechanical plate element, numerical integration
Nonlinear elasticity theory: strain measures for large deformations, stress measures
Application example: instability of bar systems using Finite Element Analysis (FEA)
Plasticity theory: flow laws (Mises, Tresca, Hill), flow rules, hardening laws
Flow laws via machine learning (ML): training and application in FEA
Introduction to python-based (pyLabFEA) and commercial FE programs (Abaqus)
Programming of bar elements with Python and verification
Analyze composite material with both commercial and python-based FE program
Buckling analysis with commercial FE program
Training ML flow laws using python-based FE program
Topology optimization with commercial FE program
assessment_rules: The graded examination can be a written exam (90 min) or an oral exam (20 min). A coursework (Studienarbeit) or a presentation (Referat) serves as an examination prerequisite. The form of the examination will be determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
